correctness.rationale: The Alexander dual consists of vertices, all unordered pairs, precisely 6N connected induced triples (2-edge paths), and N coordinate-square tetrahedra: graph is triangle-free and 4-regular, and a 5-set with every 3-subset having two edges contradicts 3|2*C(5,3)=20. Each tetrahedron has a free bent triangle; after deleting it the opposite square diagonal has a unique triangle coface. The remaining straight-path triangles each collapse with their unique distance-two chord (m,n>=5). Residual filled triangles are the square-torus triangulation, with C(N,2)-6N extra isolated edges. Thus dual is homotopy T^2 wedge that many S1, and integral Alexander duality yields Z in degree N-5 and Z^(C(N,2)-6N+2) in degree N-4. Nonzero next-to-top homology obstructs shellability of the pure cut complex. Independent graph enumeration: C5 x C5 gave 25 vertices, 50 graph edges, 150 path triples, 25 elementary squares and dual beta1=152; C5 x C6 gave (30,60,180,30), dual beta1=257.
residual_risks: Integral statement relies on valid elementary collapses and integral Alexander duality; mod-two examples alone cannot exclude torsion.
